dimensionality.warning_pca_failed_template:
**PCA of residuals could not be computed.** Reason: {reason}

Typical fixes: select at least 2 facets with ≥2 levels each, ensure every person sees multiple item-combinations, or widen your data subset. If the reason is `residual PCA was disabled by the Analysis depth setting`, re-run with Analysis depth = Standard, Full publication, or Custom > Compute residual PCA.
dimensionality.interpretation_main:
**How to interpret the PCA of standardized residuals:**

The PCA decomposes the *unexplained* variance (residuals) after the Rasch dimension
is extracted. If the data are unidimensional, residuals should be random noise and
no principal component should stand out.

| Criterion | Guideline | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| 1st eigenvalue < 2.0 | Supports unidimensionality | Linacre (2024) |
| 1st eigenvalue 2.0--3.0 | Minor secondary dimension possible; inspect content | Smith (2002) |
| 1st eigenvalue > 3.0 | Strong evidence of a secondary dimension | Linacre (2024) |
| Unexplained variance in 1st PC < 5% | Acceptable | Smith (2002) |
| Unexplained variance in 1st PC 5--10% | Investigate | Linacre (2024) |
| Eigenvalue ratio (PC1/PC2) >= 3 | Supports single dominant dimension | Reckase (1979) |

Use the scree plot below: a clear "elbow" after the 1st component, with subsequent
eigenvalues close to 1.0, supports unidimensionality.
dimensionality.warning_label_reason_template: PCA could not be computed for **{label}** — {reason}
dimensionality.insufficient_caption: Insufficient eigenvalues for dimensionality analysis (need at least 2 components).
dimensionality.assessment_minor_secondary: Minor secondary dimension possible (1st eigenvalue 2.0–3.0; Smith, 2002)
dimensionality.badge_acceptable_template: 1st eigenvalue = {ev1} -- Acceptable; monitor for secondary dimension.
dimensionality.badge_warning_template: 1st eigenvalue = {ev1} -- Possible secondary dimension. Inspect item content.

sidebar_advanced.facet_reg_caption: Regularization adds a MAP-style penalty to free non-person facet parameters. It is separate from the MML person population distribution and from full Bayesian Stan sampling.
sidebar_advanced.facet_reg_mode_light_display: Light shrinkage on all selected facets
sidebar_advanced.facet_reg_mode_help: Leave Off for the first run and for direct comparison with unpenalized FACETS/TAM-style results. Light shrinkage applies to all free levels in all selected facets; use Custom for targeted rows.
sidebar_advanced.facet_reg_no_facets_info: Select facet columns before configuring facet regularization.
sidebar_advanced.facet_reg_light_warning: Light shrinkage applies to all free levels in all selected facets and changes the estimation target. AIC/BIC remain based on the unpenalized likelihood evaluated at the regularized estimates.
sidebar_advanced.facet_reg_custom_warning: Custom regularization is a penalized fixed-effect/MAP-style estimator, not a random-effects model and not full Bayesian posterior sampling.
sidebar_advanced.facet_reg_level_help: Use * to apply to all free levels in the facet.
sidebar_advanced.enable_population_formula_help: MML-only. Replaces the zero-mean person distribution with theta_j ~ N(X_j beta, population_prior_sd^2). Current support is one-dimensional, user-set fixed variance, and main effects such as '~ grade + ses'.
sidebar_advanced.switch_to_mml_caption: Switch Estimation method to MML to enable latent regression.
sidebar_advanced.population_formula_help: '~ 1' = intercept. '~ grade + ses' = covariates. Interactions not yet supported.
sidebar_advanced.person_id_col_help: Column in the person-level table that matches the selected Person column.
sidebar_advanced.standardize_numeric_help: Centers and scales numeric covariates; same mean/SD applied to predictions.
sidebar_advanced.force_categorical_help: Comma-separated terms to dummy-code (e.g. 'grade_code, school_type'). Use to stop numeric IDs being treated as continuous.
sidebar_advanced.force_numeric_help: Comma-separated population_formula terms that must be numeric. The run stops if any listed term contains non-numeric values.
sidebar_advanced.person_data_file_help_template: Upload {file_label}. Excel uses the first worksheet.
sidebar_advanced.person_data_caption: Every fitted person must appear once in person_data when covariates are used. Categorical covariates are dummy-coded with the first level as reference.
sidebar_advanced.covariate_preview_info: Upload or paste person_data to preview numeric vs categorical covariate coding before fitting.
sidebar_advanced.intercept_only_caption: Intercept-only population model; no person-level covariate coding needed.
sidebar_advanced.covariate_preview_error_template: Covariate type preview could not be generated: {error}
sidebar_advanced.keep_original_categories_help: If checked, categories are used as-is (e.g., 1-5). If unchecked, non-consecutive categories are recoded to a contiguous internal scale.
sidebar_advanced.explicit_rating_range_help: Use this when the intended scale includes boundary categories not observed in the current data, e.g. a 1-5 scale with only 2-5 observed.
sidebar_advanced.detected_score_range_caption_template: Detected score range: {min} to {max}. Set an intended range when a category is possible but absent in this file.
sidebar_advanced.category_range_error: Max category must be larger than min category.
sidebar_advanced.noncenter_facet_help: Facet left free (not sum-to-zero). Default 'Person' = abilities float, other facets centered. Change only to free a different facet.
sidebar_advanced.dummy_facets_help: Uncentered nuisance facets — estimated but not substantively interpreted. Useful for unbalanced grouping variables that would otherwise distort the scale.
sidebar_advanced.positive_facets_help: Reverses the sign convention: higher = more positive (e.g. 'Ability'), instead of the default higher = more severe.
sidebar_advanced.maxit_help: Maximum number of optimizer iterations. Increase (e.g., 1000) if estimation does not converge.
sidebar_advanced.reltol_help: Relative tolerance for convergence. Smaller = stricter. Default 1e-6 is sufficient for most analyses.
sidebar_advanced.anchors_caption: Fix specific element measures to known values. Use when linking across administrations or when some elements have established calibrations. Format: CSV with columns **Facet, Level, Anchor** (logit value). Anchored elements are held constant; all other elements are estimated relative to them.
sidebar_advanced.anchor_file_help_template: Upload {file_label}. Required columns: Facet, Level, Anchor.
sidebar_advanced.group_anchors_caption: Constrain groups of elements to share the same measure. Use when elements belong to known groups that should be equivalent (e.g., raters trained to the same standard). Format: CSV with columns **Facet, Level, Group, GroupValue** (logit value).
sidebar_advanced.group_anchor_file_help_template: Upload {file_label}. Required columns: Facet, Level, Group, GroupValue.
sidebar_advanced.anchor_policy_help: warn shows anchor/linking issues but still estimates with valid rows. error stops estimation when any anchor audit issue is found. silent records issues in downloads/config only.
sidebar_advanced.min_common_anchors_help: Minimum anchored/common levels per facet before making linking claims.
sidebar_advanced.min_obs_per_element_help: Anchored levels below this observation count are flagged as weak.
sidebar_advanced.min_obs_per_category_help: Score categories below this count are flagged for linking/category stability.
sidebar_advanced.totalscore_help: Include elements with all-minimum or all-maximum scores in the total score calculation.
sidebar_advanced.omit_unobserved_help: Exclude elements with zero observations from the report tables.
sidebar_advanced.xtreme_help: Correction applied to extreme scores (all-min or all-max). 0 = no correction (extreme elements receive infinite estimates). 0.3-0.5 = typical correction to obtain finite estimates.
sidebar_advanced.umean_help: User-scaled mean for reported measures. Default 0.0 keeps the logit metric.

sidebar_estimation.advanced_template_caption: The template is a human-readable starting point. Convert text labels to 1-based integer arrays before calling cmdstanpy/cmdstanr, matching the generated Stan data block.
sidebar_estimation.download_advanced_template_button: Download data template for this Stan model
sidebar_estimation.q_matrix_uploader_help: First row = attribute names, first column = item names (optional).
sidebar_estimation.n_classes_help: Rost (1990) Mixture Rasch typically uses 2–3 classes.
sidebar_estimation.generate_stan_button: 📥 Generate Stan code for this advanced model
sidebar_estimation.compile_stan_locally_caption: Compile locally with cmdstan / cmdstanpy / rstan. Use this file plus your own data bundle; see the Stan Code sub-tab (Report → 💾 Exports) for a runner script.
sidebar_estimation.step_facet_help: Facet whose levels get their own threshold parameters. For GPCM, the same facet also gets slope parameters.
sidebar_estimation.gpcm_scope_caption: GPCM scope: bounded Python implementation with slope_facet = step_facet, positive slopes, and geometric mean slope fixed to 1.
sidebar_estimation.estimation_method_help: **JMLE** (Joint Maximum Likelihood): Estimates person abilities and facet parameters simultaneously using the app's analytical-gradient quasi-Newton backend. Fast but may be biased with short tests. **MML** (Marginal Maximum Likelihood): integrates over the person ability distribution with Gauss-Hermite quadrature. Guided mode uses Auto (Hybrid first, EM fallback); person abilities are computed post-hoc via EAP.
sidebar_estimation.mml_engine_help: Auto tries Hybrid first and falls back to EM if Hybrid does not converge. Hybrid starts with a few EM iterations and then switches to direct marginal-likelihood L-BFGS-B. Direct is often faster after good starts. EM is the conservative reference route.
sidebar_estimation.quad_points_help: More points improve the approximation of the person ability distribution but increase runtime. Use 7-11 for quick checks and 15+ for final review.
sidebar_estimation.population_prior_sd_help: Controls the assumed person ability distribution used by MML quadrature: theta_j ~ N(X_j beta, SD^2). This is separate from facet regularization and separate from Bayesian Stan priors.
sidebar_estimation.mml_assumptions_info_template: **MML assumptions:** Engine `{engine}`; quadrature `{quad_points}` points; person population SD fixed at `{prior_sd}`. Switch to Advanced controls to edit these settings.

data_source.teacher_paste_guide_body:
1. In your spreadsheet, keep one row per rating.
2. Include a header row such as `Student`, `Rater`, `Assignment`, `Criterion`, `Score`.
3. Select the table, copy it, and paste it here.
4. After the preview appears, map `Student` to **Person**, `Score` to **Score**, and the other columns to facets.

Do not paste total scores if rubric-level ratings are available. Blank scores are treated as missing and are excluded from the likelihood.

visuals.wright_map_caption: The Wright Map (variable map) places all persons and facet elements on a single logit scale. Persons on the left; facet elements and thresholds on the right. Good measurement requires that person abilities overlap with item/facet difficulty — large gaps indicate ceiling or floor effects.
visuals.targeting_overlap_success_template: Person and facet distributions overlap by {overlap} logits — good targeting.
visuals.targeting_overlap_warning_template: Person and facet distributions do not overlap (gap = {gap} logits) — possible ceiling or floor effect.
visuals.yardstick_intro_markdown:
**Yardstick (FACETS Table 6.0 style)**

This vertical display places all facets on a common logit ruler so you can
visually compare their relative locations. Persons are shown as a frequency
histogram on the leftmost column. Each subsequent column represents one facet.
visuals.not_enough_facets_yardstick: Not enough facets to draw a yardstick.
visuals.dense_yardstick_caption: Dense or tightly spaced yardstick: direct labels are hidden to prevent overlap. Hover points to read full labels.

report_tables.facet_regularization_warning_active: This run used MAP-style regularization on selected free facet parameters. This is penalized fixed-effect estimation, not a random-effects model and not full Bayesian sampling.
report_tables.facet_regularization_off_caption: Facet regularization was off for this run.
report_tables.eb_shrinkage_caption: Post-hoc non-person facet shrinkage; raw fitted estimates and information criteria are unchanged.
report_tables.eb_shrinkage_unavailable: EB shrinkage was requested but unavailable.
report_tables.weighting_policy_audit_caption: Documents how row weights were used or excluded before estimation and diagnostics.
report_tables.fit_warning_template: |z| >= 2 is {pct_ge2}%, well above the {threshold}% final-report benchmark. Consider reviewing data for systematic misfit.
report_tables.measurement_report_caption: **Obs. SD** = observed SD of estimates; **RMSE** = root mean square of SEs; **True SD** = √(Obs.SD² − RMSE²); **Separation (G)** = True SD / RMSE; **Strata (H)** = (4G+1)/3; **Reliability** = G²/(1+G²). See Wright & Masters (1982), Linacre (2024).

tutorial.expander_label: Tutorial: Key concepts before you begin
tutorial.section_glossary:
### Terminology glossary

| This app uses | Also known as | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Person** | Subject, Participant, Examinee, Student, Candidate | The individual being measured. In MFRM the *person* ability is the latent trait (theta) we estimate. |
| **Rater** | Judge, Assessor, Scorer, Evaluator | A human who assigns ratings. Rater severity/leniency is modeled as a facet. |
| **Task** | Item, Prompt, Topic | The stimulus or prompt that the person responds to. |
| **Criterion** | Rubric dimension, Trait, Sub-scale | A scoring dimension within a rubric (e.g., Content, Organization, Language). |
| **Facet** | — | Any systematic source of variability besides the person (rater, task, criterion, etc.). |
tutorial.section_scores:
### Raw score vs. Scale score

- **Raw score** (observed rating): the actual value assigned by a rater (e.g., 1--5 on a rubric).
  This is what appears in your *Score* column.
- **Scale score** (theta, logit measure): the estimated latent measure on the logit scale,
  produced by the Rasch/MFRM model. Scale scores are *interval-level* and comparable
  across facets, whereas raw scores are *ordinal*.

> In the output tables, **Estimate** always refers to the scale score (theta in logits),
> while **Score** or **ObsScore** refers to the original raw score.
tutorial.section_weight:
### Weight column

The optional **Weight** column lets you assign differential importance to observations.

- A weight of **1.0** (the default when no weight column is specified) treats every
  observation equally.
- Weights **> 1** increase the influence of that observation; weights **< 1** decrease it.
- Weights of **0** effectively exclude the observation from estimation.
- Typical use cases: down-weighting practice items, adjusting for unequal sample designs,
  or giving more emphasis to certain rater--task combinations.
tutorial.section_estimation_method:
### About estimation method

This app uses **JMLE** (Joint Maximum Likelihood Estimation) by default.

- **JMLE** estimates person parameters and facet parameters simultaneously
  using analytical-gradient quasi-Newton optimisation in the current
  Python backend. It does not assume a prior distribution for persons.
  This is the same broad fixed-effect estimation philosophy used by
  FACETS (Linacre, 2024).
- **MML** (Marginal Maximum Likelihood) uses the **EM algorithm**
  (Bock & Aitkin, 1981) with Gauss-Hermite quadrature:
  - **E-step**: Compute posterior P(θ_q | x_j, δ^(t)) for each person j
    at each quadrature node q, using the current item/facet estimates.
  - **M-step**: Maximise the expected complete-data log-likelihood
    Q(δ | δ^(t)) = Σ_j Σ_q r_jq log L(x_j | θ_q, δ) w.r.t. δ.
  - Iterate until the marginal log-likelihood converges (monotonic
    non-decrease guaranteed by the EM property).
  - Person abilities are computed post-hoc via **EAP** (Expected A
    Posteriori; Bock & Mislevy, 1982).
  - MML results are influenced by the *assumed prior* (normal with
    configurable fixed SD). If the true distribution deviates from normality,
    estimates may be biased. Always check whether the normality
    assumption is reasonable for your sample.
  - This is the same broad MML/EM family used by ConQuest and TAM, but this app
    uses a user-configurable fixed prior SD rather than estimating the latent
    population variance by default.

---
tutorial.section_estimation_time:
### Estimation time

Estimation may take from a few seconds to several minutes depending on:

- Number of persons, raters, tasks, and categories
- Number of observations (rows in your data)
- Convergence tolerance (`reltol`) and maximum iterations (`maxit`)

A progress spinner will be shown during estimation. Please be patient and do not
close the browser tab.
tutorial.section_missing_values:
### Missing values

Responses coded as missing are excluded from estimation (treated as structurally
absent, following FACETS conventions). Before running, use the **Missing value
recoding** panel in the sidebar to convert placeholder codes (e.g., `99`, `999`,
`N`, `NA`, `-1`, blank) into true missing values. See Linacre (2024) *A User's
Guide to FACETS*, Section 3 for details on missing data handling.

The **Response-data audit** keeps the original input row numbers and reports
whether each row entered the likelihood. Rows with missing Person, Score, or
selected facet values, non-numeric scores, or non-positive weights are excluded
before likelihood calculation; they are not recoded to zero or to any score
category.
